outcome: rates of attempted vacuum-assisted vaginal delivery
rates of successful vacuum-assisted vaginal delivery
cohort: 2,084 women with singleton gestations needing operative delivery assistance and vacuum-eligible (fully dilated, +2 station or greater, 34 weeks of gestation or greater)
finding: Among women in need of operative delivery assistance, prepregnancy obesity was associated with lower likelihood of attempted vacuum-assisted vaginal delivery but not with the success rate of the procedure if attempted.
